entries.a: GST (Goods and Services Tax) is India's tax on the supply of goods and services. It started on 1 July 2017 and replaced older taxes such as VAT, excise duty and service tax.

alts: how many GST slabs are there
entries.a: Since 22 September 2025 (GST 2.0) the main GST rates are 5% and 18%, with 40% for luxury and sin goods. Some essentials are 0%. Gold has its own 3% rate.

entries.q: What happened to the 12% and 28% GST slabs?
entries.a: GST 2.0 removed them from 22 September 2025: most 12% items moved to 5%, and most 28% items moved to 18%. Luxury and sin goods now pay 40%.

entries.q: What is the GST on gold?
alts: how much GST do I pay on gold
entries.a: Gold, including gold jewellery, coins and bars, has 3% GST on its value: 1.5% CGST + 1.5% SGST. The purity (24K, 22K or 18K) does not change the rate.

entries.q: What is the GST on making charges?
alts: tax on labour charges for jewellery
entries.a: Making charges on jewellery have 5% GST (2.5% CGST + 2.5% SGST), charged separately from the 3% GST on the gold value.

entries.q: What is the GST on silver jewellery?
entries.a: Silver jewellery and articles, like gold, have 3% GST on the metal value. Making charges have 5% GST.

entries.q: What is the GST on milk?
alts: do I charge GST on milk
entries.a: Fresh milk has no GST (0%). Since 22 September 2025, UHT milk and pre-packaged, labelled paneer also have 0% GST.

entries.q: What is the GST on ghee and butter?
entries.a: Since 22 September 2025, butter, ghee, cheese, condensed milk and milk-based drinks have 5% GST (earlier 12%). Ice cream also has 5% (earlier 18%).

entries.q: Is there GST on health insurance?
entries.a: Since 22 September 2025, individual health and life insurance policies are exempt from GST (earlier 18%).

entries.q: What are CGST, SGST and IGST?
alts: GST split between centre and state
entries.a: For a sale within the same state, GST is split equally into CGST (central) and SGST (state). For a sale to another state, the full GST is charged as IGST.

entries.q: When do I need to register for GST?
entries.a: Most businesses that sell only goods must register once yearly turnover crosses ₹40 lakh (₹20 lakh in special category states). For services the limit is ₹20 lakh (₹10 lakh in special category states).

entries.q: What is the GST composition scheme?
alts: can small businesses pay less GST
entries.a: Businesses with turnover up to ₹1.5 crore can choose the composition scheme: they pay GST at a low fixed rate (1% for traders and manufacturers), but cannot claim input tax credit or charge GST to customers.

alts: how many digits in a GST number
entries.a: A GSTIN is a business's 15-character GST number: a 2-digit state code, the 10-character PAN, an entity number, the letter Z and a check character.

alts: how does input tax credit work
entries.a: Input tax credit (ITC) lets a registered business reduce the GST it owes on sales by the GST it already paid on business purchases, as long as the supplier has filed their returns.

alts: how is GST paid to the government
entries.a: The final customer bears GST. A business collects GST on its sales, subtracts the GST it paid on purchases (input tax credit) and pays the rest to the government.
GSTR-1 is the return listing your sales. Monthly filers file it by the 11th of the next month; quarterly (QRMP) filers by the 13th of the month after the quarter.
GSTR-3B is the summary return in which you pay the GST due. Monthly filers file it by the 20th of the next month; QRMP filers by the 22nd or 24th after the quarter, depending on the state.
QRMP lets businesses with turnover up to ₹5 crore file GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B every quarter, while still paying the tax monthly.

entries.q: What is the late fee for GST returns?
entries.a: Filing GSTR-3B late costs ₹50 per day (₹20 per day for a nil return), up to a cap. Tax paid late also carries 18% interest per year.

entries.q: When is an e-way bill needed?
entries.a: An e-way bill is needed to move goods worth more than ₹50,000. Some states use a different limit for movement within the state.
E-invoicing is mandatory for B2B invoices of businesses whose yearly turnover has crossed ₹5 crore in any year since 2017-18.
An HSN code classifies goods for GST. For example, gold jewellery is under HSN 7113 and milk under HSN 0401.

alts: how to calculate GST on a price
how to remove GST from a price
entries.a: GST = price × rate ÷ 100. If the price already includes GST: GST = price × rate ÷ (100 + rate). I can work it out for you: try 'GST on 5000 at 18%'.
Karat (K) measures gold purity out of 24. 24K is about 99.9% pure, 22K is 91.6%, 18K is 75% and 14K is 58.5%.

entries.q: What is the difference between 22K and 24K gold?
entries.a: 24K gold is almost pure and very soft, so it is used for coins and bars. 22K gold (91.6%) is mixed with other metals to make it strong enough for jewellery.
916 gold is 22 karat gold: it is 91.6% pure. The number 916 appears in the BIS hallmark, for example 22K916.
A BIS hallmark certifies gold purity. It has three marks: the BIS logo, the purity (such as 22K916) and a 6-character HUID code.
HUID (Hallmark Unique Identification) is a 6-character alphanumeric code on each hallmarked piece. It is required on all hallmarked gold jewellery sold in India since 1 April 2023.

entries.q: How do I check if gold is hallmarked?
entries.a: Enter the 6-character HUID in the BIS Care app to see the item's purity, the jeweller and the assay centre that tested it.

alts: why do jewellers charge making charges
entries.a: Making charges are what a jeweller charges for crafting a piece, either a fixed amount per gram or a percentage of the gold value. They carry 5% GST.

entries.q: How is the price of gold jewellery calculated?
alts: how to calculate the cost of a gold necklace
final price of jewellery with GST
entries.a: Jewellery price = gold rate per gram × weight + making charges, then 3% GST on the gold value and 5% GST on the making charges.

entries.q: What is the gold rate today?
entries.a: I don't have live prices: I work offline and only know my built-in facts. Check today's gold rate with your supplier or a trusted market source.

entries.q: How many grams is a tola?
entries.a: A tola is a traditional unit for gold weight: about 11.66 grams. Today gold is usually priced per 10 grams.
Sterling silver is 92.5% pure silver mixed with other metals for strength. It is marked 925.

entries.q: What are fat and SNF in milk?
alts: how is milk priced by fat
entries.a: Milk is often priced by fat and SNF (solids-not-fat). Fat is the butterfat; SNF is the protein, lactose and minerals. Higher fat and SNF usually earn a higher price.

entries.q: How much fat is in cow and buffalo milk?
alts: difference between cow and buffalo milk
entries.a: Cow milk usually has about 3.5 to 5% fat, and buffalo milk about 6 to 8%. Buffalo milk also has more SNF.

entries.q: How should raw milk be stored?
entries.a: Cool raw milk to 4°C or below soon after milking and sell or process it quickly. Clean and sanitise cans and the milking machine after every use.
A lead is a person or business who might buy from you, such as a past customer, a referral or someone who asked about your products. Ask me to 'find leads' and I'll suggest ways.

entries.q: How can I get more customers?
alts: how to get more customers for my shop
entries.a: Ask happy customers for referrals, win back past customers, reach out on birthdays and anniversaries, and keep your customer list up to date. Ask me to 'find leads' and I'll suggest three ways to start.

entries.q: How do I calculate profit margin?
entries.a: Profit margin = (selling price - cost) ÷ selling price × 100. Example: cost ₹80 and price ₹100 give a 20% margin.
Markup = (selling price - cost) ÷ cost × 100. Example: cost ₹80 and price ₹100 give a 25% markup, but a 20% margin.

entries.q: What is the difference between gross profit and net profit?
entries.a: Gross profit = sales - cost of the goods sold. Net profit = gross profit - all other expenses such as rent, salaries and taxes.
The break-even point is where sales cover all costs. Break-even units = fixed costs ÷ (price per unit - variable cost per unit).
Turnover is the total value of your sales in a period, before any costs are subtracted.
Cash flow is the money coming in and going out of your business over a period. Positive cash flow means more comes in than goes out.
Working capital is the money for daily operations: current assets (cash, stock, money owed to you) minus current liabilities (bills you must pay soon).
Inventory is the stock you hold to sell. Tracking it helps you reorder on time and avoid dead stock.
An invoice is a bill listing what was sold, the price, the tax and the total. A GST invoice also shows the GSTINs, the HSN code and the GST split.
PAN (Permanent Account Number) is a 10-character ID from the Income Tax Department. It is needed for GST registration, income tax returns and large transactions.
Udyam registration is the free government registration for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). It can help with loans and government schemes.
UPI lets customers pay instantly from their bank account by scanning a QR code or entering a UPI ID.

entries.q: How much is a lakh and a crore?
alts: how many zeros in a lakh
how many zeros in a crore
entries.a: 1 lakh = 1,00,000 (one hundred thousand). 1 crore = 1,00,00,000 (ten million), which is 100 lakh.
